findings.finding: The long spectrum rectangle, narrow perpendicular detector, full-length endpoint extensions, outward l arrows, lower strip projections and inward Delta l arrows are all present. In drawing coordinates, l spans x=60..585 and Delta l spans x=212..236. The latter is the detector width within the former, not a uniform frequency scale.

At 640 px, all five labels and their intended targets are distinguishable, with no clipping or text overlap. The source's solid dark strip is modernized as a gray filled strip; its location and width remain clear. Red/violet are English endpoint labels, not literal ink-color requirements.

Both complete n103 editions explicitly distinguish position length l from frequency interval Delta nu and require calibration. The figure adds neither frequency values nor an equal-distance/equal-frequency claim.

findings.finding: The one preview directly shows five outlined marks then one solid mark, six separate dashed drops, five intermediate ticks, and the two red/violet endpoint lines. No numerical axis values, extra sample, missing guide or sixth hollow mark is present.

The rightward frequency and upward Delta E/Delta t axes share one frame. The solid curve decreases and flattens from the red boundary to the violet boundary. Each sample sits on a cubic-join coordinate of the SVG curve: (200,137), (260,185), (320,211), (380,229), (440,244), (500,256) in SVG coordinates. Endpoints are (170,90) and (530,263); the curve does not extend outside the visible-band interval.

Both complete n103 editions qualify this as the book's arc-lamp visible-band experiment, not every source or the full electromagnetic spectrum. They require frequency calibration and equal bandwidths or correction. Clean sample/tick spacing is declared schematic regularization, not invented measured data.

The stacked energy/time fraction, frequency symbol and two English endpoint labels are legible at 640 px. Source Chinese endpoint subscripts are translated without altering red-before-violet ordering.

opticalRelationshipEvidence.prismContinuity: For each height, collimated-ray-i ends at (296,y), prism-transmission-ray-i connects (296,y) to (320,y), and both wavelength rays start at (320,y). Both combined paths cross the triangular prism's sloping faces; neither runs below its base.

findings.finding: The one current prism-repair preview preserves the slit/collimator, both convex lenses, central prism and housing, and the rear screen. Two divergent slit rays become parallel after L1. The current candidate includes continuous prism traversal connections; both rays visibly traverse the prism rather than bypassing it.

Each same-wavelength pair has identical pre-L2 direction vectors. After L2, both red paths meet the red mark and both violet paths meet the separate lower violet mark on the same screen. This is focusing into separate slit images, not arbitrary separating lines, a single shared focus, or parallel rays continuing unfocused onto the screen.

All five source labels have recognizable modern English/mathematical counterparts at 640 px. Red/Violet labels remain distinguishable next to the two screen images. Lens fills obscure the short in-glass ray sections, but the external paths visibly arrive at and depart from the appropriate lenses; they are not unsupported floating segments.

This is accepted as the editions' qualitative instrument schematic, not a scale Snell-law construction: wavelength splitting is drawn inside the prism, and no refractive indices, interface-angle measurements, focal lengths or physical dimensions are asserted. The retained instructional relationships are collimation, prism traversal, parallel color bundles, greater violet displacement and separate L2 screen images.
